verdict.rationale: Terraform's GitHub README says it builds a graph of all resources and parallelizes creation and modification of non-dependent resources. A single plan/apply executes every proposed operation across the whole configuration and can run non-interactively with -auto-approve, so bulk changes across many items are core to how it works. A community user credits it with making operations at scale possible. Missing for 10: documentation of bulk-definition constructs (e.g. count/for_each), selective bulk targeting or bulk state manipulation, and hands-on evidence of large-scale bulk runs.
